headline: Correction: KEPCO's October leak also exposed staff face-recognition data, not only names and phone numbers.
summary: What was wrong: c009 said the October leak covered names, affiliations and phone numbers only. What is right now: Yonhap (Oct 23, already cited) and The Leaves (Oct 20) report that coded face-recognition data of about 400 staff from the head-office entry system was also exposed. c009 stays Reported.
author: Research agent

headline: More detail on KEPCO's October breach, including staff face-recognition data; its findings are not yet public.
summary: New Tier 2 sources on the separate October breach: Yonhap (Oct 4) says the exposed page was not public and the data came down about 32 hours after KEPCO noticed; Yonhap (Oct 23) and The Leaves (Oct 20) say coded face-recognition data of about 400 staff was also exposed (see the correction entry); The Leaves alone adds 14,957 CCTV equipment access records and says investigators were weighing a partner-company route and outside hacking. Newspim (Nov 6) quoted KEPCO saying investigators' October findings were due in mid-November; none are public (c010, q005 still open). Wording fix: SRM staff data includes mobile numbers (c004, q002). No statement yet from the privacy regulator, police, ministry or intelligence service; no new KEPCO notice. Main answer unchanged. Privacy check done: no officials, lawmakers, hotlines or emails added.
author: Research agent

headline: KEPCO's own procurement-system notice confirms what SRM data leaked.
summary: New Tier 1 source: KEPCO's SRM leak notice (Nov 22) says outside illegal access on Nov 20 leaked staff and supplier data and lists the items, so c004 moves from Reported to Confirmed and the what-data question (q002) from Reported to Confirmed. The notice gives no counts; those still come from outlets relaying KEPCO. New Tier 2: the Kukmin Daily, with Financial News, quotes KEPCO saying it became a target as it expanded open services such as simplified authentication (c007). How the attacker got in is still not established. No statement yet from the privacy regulator, police, ministry or intelligence service. Main answer unchanged. Privacy check done: no officials, hotlines or emails added.
author: Research agent

headline: News1 reports the leak was noticed through slow access and dark-web signs; KEPCO's spring audit had found 218 severe weaknesses.
summary: New Tier 2 sources: News1 says the breach came to light through access delays and dark-web indications (c016, Reported). Money Today reported on Oct 19 that KEPCO's own April to July security review rated 218 weaknesses severe, including in all 10 public services tested (c017, Reported; no public link to either breach). DailySecu's follow-up notes KEPCO has not addressed the dark-web post (c013). c007 updated. How the attacker got in is still not established. No statement yet from the privacy regulator, police, ministry or intelligence service. Main answer unchanged. Privacy check done: no officials, lawmakers, poster names or hotlines added.
author: Research agent

headline: Press reports a dark-web post claiming KEPCO data a day before KEPCO detected the breach; ministry says power supply not affected.
summary: Two outlets (DailySecu, ZDNet Korea) report a Nov 19 dark-web forum post claiming KEPCO user, supplier and bidding data (c013, Reported); the claim that contract records were taken is Unverified and KEPCO denies it (c014). Seoul Economic Daily gives KEPCO's timeline (aware 6 AM Nov 20, police asked 12:31 PM Nov 20, privacy regulator filing 6:30 PM Nov 22) and reports the climate ministry says power operations are not affected (c015, Reported; new q006). c005, c007, c008, c011 updated. 7 new Tier 2 sources. Main answer unchanged. Privacy check done: the poster's forum name and KEPCO hotlines left out.
author: Research agent

headline: KEPCO's own notices say a cyber intrusion caused the leak; police were asked to investigate.
summary: Found KEPCO's own apology and KEPCO ON leak notice (Tier 1) on kepco.co.kr. They state a cyber intrusion and outside illegal access attempts, list the leaked KEPCO ON items, and say police were asked to investigate, settling an earlier conflict. c001, c003, c005, c006 and c011 move from Reported to Confirmed; c007 updated; c012 added (Aju Press: registration and card numbers stored encrypted, Reported). 6 new sources (2 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2). On editor review, the main answer (q001) moves from Reported to Confirmed because KEPCO's own notices state a cyber intrusion; how the attacker got in and who it was remain not established. Privacy check done.
author: Research agent

headline: KEPCO says an outside attacker took data on about 1.52 million users; claims are Reported, cause not established.
summary: First draft. 7 sources (all Tier 2), 11 claims, 5 questions. KEPCO says an outside attacker took data on about 1.52 million users from KEPCO ON and the SRM procurement system. All of it is Reported, since we read only outlets relaying the company's statement. The method, attacker and any link to the October breach are Not established. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
